notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 58-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.66, creatinine 0.91-0.93, hemoglobin 10.7-12.6, platelets 235-238, sodium 140-141, wbc 7.6-7.9; vitals dbp 76-80, heart_rate 75-79, map 91-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 120-126, spo2 97-98, temp 36.8-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.91-0.95, hemoglobin 9.7-10.5, platelets 234-240, sodium 140-141, wbc 7.3-7.9; vitals dbp 75-78, heart_rate 74-79, map 91-94, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 121-125, spo2 97-99, temp 36.7-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 58-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
